items.title: Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: I met Donald Brown who is a magnificent pianist, but he was teaching there and he was a current member of the Messengers. And I became very closely in his company. I followed him everywhere. I would go see him places play, I would go sit in with him

ctx.x: So let’s talk about Art Blakey and composing. I’m thinking of you taking a tune to Mr. Blakey and why would he like something and not something else?

Well one thing that was unique about Art Blakey, he didn’t dislike anything. He would take any individual’s music and make it work for the ensemble. He might have a suggestion or he might have some constructive criticism, but by and large I never saw Art just dismiss a song. He would find a way to rehearse it, we’d play it a couple of times. Now if he liked it it would get played more maybe than someone else’s compositions, but I never knew Art — because he really encouraged everyone to write music. So in that…
Do you know if — a lot of those fellows who started out with him did that training — did most of them leave to become leaders themselves or did he tell them, “Look time for you to move on”?
